title: As a founder, domain search is fast and honest — instant availability, alternate TLD suggestions, and no lookup-then-squat games on names I searched
As a developer, I can check domain availability programmatically — a documented check/search API my code or agent can call with clear rate limits
As a power user, the registrar carries the TLDs I actually want — hundreds of extensions with any special requirements (restricted TLDs, country codes) documented per TLD
As a power user, premium and aftermarket domains are first-class — premium pricing shown in search, and a marketplace or broker path for taken names
As a developer, I can register a domain end to end via the API — purchase, contacts, and nameservers in documented calls, so registration can be part of a deploy script
As a power user, transferring domains IN is documented and honest — EPP/auth-code flow, status tracking, what the transfer costs, and what happens to remaining registration time
As an IT admin, renewals never surprise me — auto-renew controls per domain, expiry notices, and documented grace/redemption windows if something lapses
As a power user managing a portfolio, bulk operations are real — bulk search, registration, renewal, nameserver changes, and transfers across many domains at once
As a developer, full DNS hosting comes with the domain — every record type, low TTLs, and a management UI that doesn't fight me
As a developer, DNS records are CRUD-able via a documented API — create, update, and delete records programmatically for automation and ACME challenges
As a security engineer, DNSSEC is supported and easy — one-click or API-driven signing with the DS records handled at the registry
As a privacy-first user, WHOIS privacy is free and on by default — my name, address, and email stay redacted without an upsell
As a security engineer, my domains can be locked down — transfer lock by default and a registry-lock option for the domains that must never move
As a security engineer, the registrar account itself is defensible — real 2FA, scoped API credentials, and IP allowlisting on API access
As a founder, the full price list is published — registration, renewal, and transfer priced separately per TLD, with no teaser first-year price hiding a renewal spike
As a power user, pricing is at or near wholesale — at-cost claims backed by visible registry fee breakdowns or a published low-margin guarantee
As a developer, pricing is machine-readable — an API or feed returns current registration/renewal/transfer prices per TLD so tooling can compare and budget
As a developer, I can get API credentials self-serve and test safely — a sandbox or test environment where registrations don't cost real money
As a founder, the basics are bundled — email forwarding on my domain and free SSL so the parked-to-launched path costs nothing extra
As a founder, connecting the domain to where my site lives is one guided step — templates or one-click connect for the major hosts and platforms
